papers.abstract: We study the large-time relative entropy of a Poisson average $P_t* $ relative to the translated Poisson kernel $P_t( - )$ with matching mean. The Cayley transform normalizes the problem by pulling normalized Haar measure on the circle back to the Cauchy law on~$ $, and this normalization is rigid among orientation-preserving $C^1$ charts. In the Cayley variable the ratio \[ R_ (y)= 1+y^2 1+(y- )^2 \] has a finite Chebyshev--Fourier mode calculus. The mode parity eliminates odd powers through the finite expansion order, and the uniform remainder estimates give an expansion of $D_ KL (P_t* \,\|\,P_t( - ))$ through order~$t^ -8 $ under a finite centred seventh absolute moment. The sixth- and eighth-order coefficients admit explicit non-negative defect coordinates. A separate rigidity corollary identifies the symmetric two-point law as the unique coefficient extremizer, and the eighth-order defect strictly amplifies the sixth-order one with equality only at that law. papers.abstract: We consider two coarse-observation problems, one arithmetic and one operator-algebraic, both governed by the question of what remains visible after passing to a quotient. On the arithmetic side we work under an abstract Chebotarev spectral expansion for primitive counts, together with the corresponding Artin factorization. For quotients of finite abelian groups we prove an exact chain rule for relative entropy and an orthogonal decomposition of the \( ^2\)-defect into quotient-visible and quotient-invisible Fourier energy. The full quotient profile then determines, by Möbius inversion on the subgroup lattice, the Fourier mass carried by characters with prescribed exact kernel; the family of quotient relative entropies recovers the same information to second order. papers.title: Finite-window Zeckendorf normalization, compatible restriction, and the pair shift
papers.status: 待分诊
papers.board_row: — | 待分诊 | —
papers.abstract: We study finite-window Zeckendorf normalization for binary words in Fibonacci weights. Given a word of length \(m\), its Fibonacci value is replaced by the Zeckendorf expansion and then truncated back to the original window. This defines an idempotent map onto the length-\(m\) language of the golden-mean shift, but it does not commute with naive restriction when the window size varies. There is nevertheless a unique compatible restriction on microstates, and the discrepancy from naive truncation may occupy the whole visible window; in particular, no uniformly bounded tail correction can restore commutation. A structural theorem is proved for zero-synchronized local normalizers of rewrite span \(r\): the associated interior pair language of raw and normalized digits is always a synchronized sofic shift whose follower memory is at most \(r-1\). The Fibonacci rule \(011 100\) is the span-\(3\) case, and its follower graph collapses canonically to the four-state pair shift studied in th...

papers.abstract: Let \(Y\) be a topologically mixing one-step subshift of finite type, \( _ \) the equilibrium Markov measure of a one-step potential, \(H\) a Markov hole. This paper is centered on one finite-state theorem for first-entry residue events into \(H\): the Bayes error of a depth-\(m\) observation is exactly a killed-matrix path sum with residue-dependent terminal ambiguity weights. papers.title: Adams--M\"obius primitive inversion for finite-group extensions of shifts of finite type
papers.board_row: ETDS | 已投 05-10 | ScholarOne ETDS; Oracle+Claude pass, 9 rounds
papers.abstract: For finite-group extensions of mixing subshifts of finite type, we develop a primitive determinant calculus in Peter--Weyl coordinates. The main theorem spine is finite-group theoretic. First, twisted determinants, which record periodic labels, are converted into primitive Peter--Weyl series by an Adams--M\"obius inversion that accounts for the operations \(g g^m\) produced by repetitions of primitive orbits. Second, under the gap hypothesis, those primitive series have well-defined Perron-point values, giving conjugacy-class Mertens constants; Hermitian character orthogonality then reads off the non-trivial primitive channels from the constant deviations. The linear span of cyclic quotient observables is the one-dimensional shadow of the full primitive class profile at the Perron point, under \( < \). The root-of-unity layer used for scalar sampling is separate: it appears only after replacing the cocycle by the canonical cyclic lift. The orthogonal complement is a genuine non-abel...

papers.abstract: We prove that the fiber multiplicities of finite-window Zeckendorf stabilization are Fibonacci-lag discrete derivatives of the classical Fibonacci partition function. The collision moments $S_q(m)= _ x d_m(x)^q$ are thereby squeezed between adjacent Fibonacci windows of Sanna's partition power sums, yielding $S_q(m) _q _q^m$ for every $q 1$. A finite-state kernel realization identifies each $ _q$ ($q 2$) as the Perron root of a nonnegative integer matrix of polynomial size, proving that $ _q$ is an algebraic integer. The sequence $P_q= _q$ (with $P_0= $) is convex, and its discrete slopes $ _q=P_q-P_ q-1 $ select the canonical thickness bands of the model: the $q$-canonical law is exponentially concentrated on $[ _q, _ q+1 ]$, with two-sided exponential estimates for band cardinality and visible mass. Diverging tilts select the zero-temperature thickness $ 12 $, recovering $D_m^ 1/m $ and the diagonal high-moment asymptotic. In the arithmetic window $q=9, ,17$, explicit exact-kernel...

papers.abstract: We consider a finite symbolic map from binary rotation words to the golden-mean language, obtained by taking a Fibonacci valuation, passing to Zeckendorf normal form and truncating the resulting prefix. Star-discrepancy estimates for irrational rotations give explicit total-variation and relative entropy bounds for the empirical laws of these folded words. In the Sturmian case \( = \), the map has a stronger property: on the realized length-\(m\) language it is injective, and the induced process is conjugate to the usual \(m\)-block presentation of the Sturmian subshift. The comparison with the golden-mean Parry block law can then be made at fixed resolution. We give an exact identity for \( ( \| _m)\), determine the support-constrained minima for all R\'enyi orders, and, for \(m 6\), identify the optimal injective placement of the Sturmian factor law in the golden-mean language. papers.abstract: We study gluing failure for references evaluated at information states in a focused note that starts from a chosen local-object layer and an explicit gluing-sensitive realization-prestack hypothesis, rather than from a canonical obstruction theory on a bare set-valued presheaf. Naming an abelian band is not an existence theorem for such a prestack. The split lift is only a separatedness criterion: for $ , F_ p,s (U)$ its isomorphism presheaf on the slice $ C_a/U$ is \[ V cases (V), & _V^U( )= _V^U( ),\\ , & _V^U( ) _V^U( ), cases \] so it may have mixed support. Hence the split lift is a prestack for the original presheaf exactly when equality in $F_ p,s |_ C_a $ is separated. After sheafifying $F_ p,s $ the same split construction realizes the sheafified visible classes, not the original presheaf unless the relevant comparison map is an isomorphism. papers.title: Golden-Mean Folding in Binary Scan--Projection Systems:\ Types, Normal Forms, and Auditable Addressing
papers.abstract: Finite-window observations in symbolic dynamics, coding theory, automata, and auditable computation naturally generate exponentially large binary microstate spaces \( _m=\ 0,1\ ^m\). If microstates are used directly as types, increasing the resolution \(m\) produces sparsity, representational instability, and poor cross-scale comparability. This paper studies scan--projection systems induced by a singly generated action \(T^t:X X\) and a binary readout \(s_t(x)= _W(T^t x)\), and constructs a golden-mean folding mechanism that maps microstates \( _m\) to stable type spaces \(X_m\). Using Fibonacci/Zeckendorf syntax, we define the fold by the residue section \[ _m( )=s_m (N_m( ) F_ m+2 ), \] and prove that it is well-defined, computable, idempotent, and surjective. Thus every finite-window microstate admits a unique stable normal form. papers.abstract: We study gluing failure in a forcing semantics whose states are sets of realizations. For an admitted reference, compatible local sectionability gives nonemptiness of the sheafification of the associated local-object functor, and the converse holds on slice-separated reference slices. We also prove a lower-fragment separation theorem on the admitted subdomain: in the automorphism-invariant, constant-free, one-variable fragment of the lower reduct, the predicates for compatible local sections, global sections, and gluing-level nullity are undefinable in that fragment. At the groupoid-valued level, a representative-rigid realization prestack that is globally conservative at the terminal fibre forces surjectivity of the sheafification unit there under slice-separatedness; under $H^1$-vanishing and the same slice-separatedness, this is equivalent to the local object functor already being a sheaf at that fibre, so gluing-level nullity cannot be recovered from a strict functorial choice o...

papers.title: Joukowsky Elliptic Gates, G\"odel--Lorentz Algebraization,\\ and $p$-Adic Spectral Rigidity
papers.status: 待分诊
papers.board_row: — | 待分诊 | —
papers.abstract: We study two families of Joukowsky-type maps that send the unit circle to confocal ellipses and extract from them arithmetic, algebraic, and potential-theoretic invariants. First, for the elliptic projection gates \(J_ c,m (e^ i )=e^ im +c e^ -im \), we prove a sharp Fourier support theorem for the logarithmic speed, identify its \(p\)-adic slope invariants, and show that the full spectral data uniquely reconstruct the rational parameter \(c\) and the covering multiplicity \(m\). Second, we algebraize prime-register data by a homomorphism into \( SO ^+(1,1)\), obtaining Lorentz-type composition laws, condition-number identities, and primorial extremality statements for associated ellipses and ellipsoids. Third, for the two-scale transport polynomial generated by \(J_r(z)=rz+r^ -1 z^ -1 \), we establish pullback and discriminant factorizations, derive Lee--Yang elliptic Mahler/free-energy identities, and prove holographic reconstruction results from a single transport scale.

papers.abstract: Classical density theory for regular languages implies that normalized length-\(m\) counts for a fixed DFA are eventually periodic up to an exponentially small error. This paper turns that input into quantitative finite-budget obstructions for approximating prime slices by one fixed DFA, and extends the comparison to arbitrary trim deterministic presentations with several maximal components. papers.title: Finite-Window Zeckendorf Fibers and the\\ Discrete Thermodynamics of Fibonacci Partition Differences
papers.abstract: We prove that the fiber multiplicities of finite-window Zeckendorf stabilization are Fibonacci-lag discrete derivatives of the classical Fibonacci partition function. The collision moments $S_q(m)= _ x d_m(x)^q$ are thereby squeezed between adjacent Fibonacci windows of Sanna's partition power sums, yielding $S_q(m) _q _q^m$ for every $q 1$. A finite-state kernel realization identifies each $ _q$ ($q 2$) as the Perron root of a nonnegative integer matrix of polynomial size and hence proves that $ _q$ is an algebraic integer. The pressure sequence $p_q= _q$ (with $p_0= $) is convex, and its discrete slopes $ _q=p_q-p_ q-1 $ select the canonical thickness bands of the model: the $q$-canonical law is exponentially concentrated on $[ _q, _ q+1 ]$, with two-sided exponential estimates for band cardinality and visible mass. Diverging tilts select the zero-temperature thickness $ 12 $, so the largest fiber size $D_m$ satisfies $D_m^ 1/m $ and the diagonal high-moment asymptotic follows. We...

papers.abstract: We present an expository note on recursive addressing. Starting from a measurable dynamical system and a finite family of observable concepts, we record the standard fact that recursively generated address cylinders refine visible information without enlarging the visible $ $-algebra. Fixing a time origin, the induced symbolic coding produces admissible words and cylinder objects for a prefix site. Within this language, address failure splits into the standard presheaf-theoretic phenomena of empty local fibers, descent failure, and non-separatedness. For a finite cover together with local readout objects carrying an abelian band, we define the associated intrinsic C ech defect class and the visible quotient obtained by killing that class. papers.abstract: We study how refinement of prefix information changes the optimal decision error for a measurable event. For an increasing prefix filtration, the scan error profile is the smallest classification error achievable by rules that see only depth-$m$ information. We give an exact atomwise Bayes decomposition and a threshold-convexity compensator identity for this profile, then apply these filtration tools to symbolic systems. For Parry measures, a finite follower-resolving observer graph determines the ambiguity exponent from finite-state data and gives a uniform boundary-thickness constant under a bounded resolving window. For H\"older Gibbs states, the refined ambiguous graph carries an event-relative boundary pressure: its reachable recurrent components determine the weighted boundary partition sums, and under the observer-regular/resolving hypothesis the pressure gap transfers to the scan-error decay rate. papers.title: Finite Observation and Escape Rates\\ for Markov Holes in Mixing Shifts of Finite Type
papers.abstract: Let \(Y\) be a topologically mixing one-step subshift of finite type, \( _ \) the equilibrium Markov measure of a one-step potential, and \(H\) a Markov hole with mixing survivor subshift \(Y_H\). We introduce the depth-\(m\) Bayes error of first-entry residue events into \(H\) as a new observable for open symbolic dynamics and show that it admits an exact killed-matrix path sum: it is asymptotic to survivor mass up to a residue-dependent quasistationary amplitude, and its exponential rate recovers the escape rate \( _H( )=P_Y( )-P_ Y_H ( )\). The paper is deliberately finite-state: the escape-rate formula, Perron--Frobenius asymptotics for the killed matrix, and Chen--Stein Poisson approximation are standard inputs, whereas the Bayes-error observable and its residue-dependent ambiguity amplitude are the new features. papers.abstract: We study the finite-window Fibonacci normalization which sends a binary word of length $m$ to the unique golden-mean admissible word with the same Fibonacci valuation modulo $F_ m+2 $. The map is usually many-to-one on a single window, but its sliding overlap extension has a sharp threshold. We prove that for every $m 3$ it is a finite-memory conjugacy from the full two-shift onto a subshift of finite type, with an explicit decoder. For $m=2$ the only nontrivial path-space fiber is the pair of constant sequences; this yields exact conditional-entropy and Kullback--Leibler defect formulas and a mod-zero inverse off the branch. The proof combines a bi-resolving overlap presentation with a residue decoder, so the degree-one conclusion is an arithmetic fact rather than a formal consequence of resolving theory. Within the constant-type metallic model of Definition~ , we also show that the golden case is exceptional: every integer parameter $A 2$ is already invertible at window length two...

papers.abstract: We separate three kinds of structure that are easily conflated in single-primitive representation results. Expression universality requires only terms over one binary operation; Odrzywo ek's operation \(e^x- Log y\) gives such terms for a standard elementary library. Protocol universality adds computable normal forms and readout maps. With Zeckendorf normal forms and the classical Church-iteration identities we obtain a protocol for \(+\) and \( \) on \( \), and we show that multiplication cannot be read on one free monogenic orbit by the ambient product, even after an injective recoding. Finite fibers give Hankel-positive collision moments and finite Prony reconstruction, but they do not force a finite-state transfer law: computable finite-fiber covers may preserve the normal forms and readouts while having second moments of superexponential growth. papers.abstract: For each positive integer $n$, let $B_n$ denote the set of divisors of the Fibonacci number $F_n$ whose rank of apparition equals~$n$. We prove that $B_n$ is an upper set in the divisor lattice of $F_n$ obtained by removing the covering ideals associated with the maximal proper divisors of~$n$. Our main result classifies the minimal generators of~$B_n$: every minimal generator factors uniquely as a pairwise coprime product of atomic prime-power birth moduli forming a witness cover whose support spans the prime coordinates of~$n$. This yields the sharp bound $ (m) (n)$ for every minimal generator $m$, with equality for every odd $n 3$, and a primitive-versus-ladder dichotomy for atomic factors. We give complete classifications for $ (n) 3$ and show that both $B_n$ and its minimal-generator set admit unique factorizations into connected coordinate blocks, producing partition-lattice formulas for $A(n) = \#B_n$ and $\# M _n$. papers.title: Spectral Rigidity of Hypercube Lumpability\\ and Fold Gauge Homology
papers.status: 待分诊
papers.board_row: — | 待分诊 | —
papers.abstract: We study coarse-grainings of the simple random walk on the hypercube and prove a spectral rigidity principle for equitable lumpings: every quotient eigenvalue must belong to the discrete hypercube spectrum \(\ 1-2k/m:0 k m\ \). Applied to the audited bin-fold pushforward kernel in window \(6\), this yields a sharp falsifier for hidden-state-free strong lumpability, because the observed nontrivial eigenvalues fall outside the hypercube grid. We then show that permutation-natural binary jump structures on boundary uplift fibers are uniquely controlled by the sign character, giving rise to orientation torsors with explicit product, subset, and wreath formulas. Finally, we compute low-degree homology of the associated fold-gauge groups, analyze chiral compression of hypercube sectors, and quantify the entropy cost of fiberwise free involutions and one-bit statistical tests.

papers.title: Zeckendorf Stable Arithmetic:\\ Fibonacci Congruence, Field Phases, and Online Algorithms
papers.status: 待分诊
papers.board_row: — | 待分诊 | —
papers.abstract: We study arithmetic induced by Zeckendorf representations and show that the relevant algebraic structure is forced by local Fibonacci rewriting rather than inserted a priori. Starting from the free commutative monoid of scale-counting configurations, we quotient by the Fibonacci relations and prove that the resulting monoid is canonically isomorphic to \( \), with the Zeckendorf language furnishing a unique computable normal representative in each class. At finite resolution \(m\), the stable value map \(V_m:X_m /(F_ m+2 )\) transports addition and multiplication to a commutative ring structure on \(X_m\), yielding field phases when \(F_ m+2 \) is prime and Chinese-remainder decompositions when it is composite. We then connect this algebraic picture with online Zeckendorf addition, multiplicative generation by iteration, and a Fibonacci-adic inverse-limit ring obtained from the divisibility chain \(F_ 2^k F_ 2^ k+1 \).

papers.abstract: We study the canonical normalization map behind addition in Zeckendorf numeration. Digitwise superposition of two admissible Zeckendorf words yields a finitely supported word over $\ 0,1,2\ $, and addition is recovered by replacing this overlay with the unique admissible word of the same Fibonacci value. We realize this normalization as the canonical section of a Fibonacci congruence and describe it by a terminating local rewrite system whose irreducible configurations are exactly the admissible Zeckendorf words. We then separate this one-sided low-to-high canonical normalizer from the classical most-significant-digit-first adders of Frougny and Berstel. In the one-sided model, the canonical map has coordinatewise unbounded anticipation, is not subsequential, and has exact prefix-destruction index $ (n)=n$. We prove that $B_n$ is an upper set in the divisor lattice of $F_n$ obtained by removing the covering ideals associated with the maximal proper divisors of~$n$. Our main result classifies the minimal generators of~$B_n$: every minimal generator factors uniquely as a pairwise coprime product of atomic prime-power birth moduli forming a witness cover whose support spans the prime coordinates of~$n$. papers.abstract: For each $m 1$, let $ _m:\ 0,1\ ^m X_m$ send a binary word to the first $m$ digits of the Zeckendorf expansion of its Fibonacci value. We show that $ _m$ is the normal-form map of a finite terminating confluent rewrite system and that the family $( _m)_ m 1 $ is compatible with restriction in $m$. For $m 3$ we prove that the associated sliding block code $ _m$ has the following exact reconstruction property: every block of $n m$ consecutive output symbols has a unique binary preimage of length $n+m-1$. Equivalently, the block map $B_ m,n :\ 0,1\ ^ n+m-1 L_n(Y_m)$ is a bijection and $ L_n(Y_m) =2^ n+m-1 $. Equivalently, for $m 3$ the residue vector modulo $F_ m+2 $ of the overlapping local Fibonacci sums determines the entire binary block uniquely. This block bijection gives local inverse rules with memory $r$ and anticipation $m-1-r$ for every $0 r m-1$, and the one-sided inverse memory $m-1$ is best possible. papers.title: Folded Histograms of Irrational Rotations: Sampling Certificates and Structural Mismatch to the Parry Measure
papers.abstract: We propose a two-stage audit framework for coarse-grained orbit data and work it out completely in one explicit benchmark. The benchmark is a deterministic fold that sends finite binary words from an irrational rotation to the golden-mean shift by Fibonacci weighting and Zeckendorf normalization. The first stage asks whether an empirical folded histogram is already close to its deterministic folded limit law; the second asks whether the same histogram is compatible with a natural ambient equilibrium, here the Parry block law. In the canonical Sturmian slice \( = \), the induced sequence map is topologically conjugate to the classical higher-block presentation of the Sturmian source, so the fold is dynamically lossless on realized orbit data. This makes the benchmark unusually explicit. We obtain closed formulas for \( ( \| _m)\), exact support-constrained minima for all Renyi orders, and, for all sufficiently large \(m\), the optimal injective relabeling of the realized Sturmian law...

papers.title: Finite-window rigidity in Fibonacci numeration
papers.abstract: For each $m 1$, let $ _m:\ 0,1\ ^m X_m$ send a binary word to the first $m$ digits of the Zeckendorf expansion of its Fibonacci value. We show that $ _m$ is the normal-form map of a finite terminating confluent rewrite system and that the family $( _m)_ m 1 $ is compatible with restriction in $m$. For $m 3$ we prove that the associated sliding block code $ _m$ has the following exact reconstruction property: every block of $n m$ consecutive output symbols has a unique binary preimage of length $n+m-1$. Equivalently, the block map $B_ m,n :\ 0,1\ ^ n+m-1 L_n(Y_m)$ is a bijection and $ L_n(Y_m) =2^ n+m-1 $. Equivalently, for $m 3$ the residue vector modulo $F_ m+2 $ of the overlapping local Fibonacci sums determines the entire binary block uniquely. This block bijection gives local inverse rules with memory $r$ and anticipation $m-1-r$ for every $0 r m-1$, and the one-sided inverse memory $m-1$ is best possible. papers.title: A sharp three-window threshold and finite-memory conjugacy in Fibonacci stabilization
papers.abstract: We study the canonical Fibonacci stabilization map \[ _m:\ 0,1\ ^m X_m, \] which sends a binary word to the unique admissible Fibonacci word with the same valuation modulo $F_ m+2 $. The local map is many-to-one on isolated windows, but the relevant question is whether this ambiguity survives under sliding overlap. We prove a sharp threshold at $m=3$. For every $m 3$, the overlapping stabilized-window map is injective, admits an explicit finite-memory inverse, and identifies its image with a subshift of finite type topologically conjugate to the full two-shift. At $m=2$, the failure of injectivity is completely concentrated on a unique branch orbit; this yields exact formulas for the conditional entropy and Kullback--Leibler defect and implies mod-zero invertibility off the branch set. On the arithmetic side, stabilization fibers admit an exact residue characterization and a discrete Fourier formula, and their second moment satisfies a linear recurrence. papers.abstract: For each positive integer $n$, let $B_n$ denote the set of divisors of the Fibonacci number $F_n$ whose rank of apparition equals~$n$. We prove that $B_n$ is an upper set in the divisor lattice of $F_n$ obtained by removing the covering ideals associated with the maximal proper divisors of~$n$, and that every minimal generator factors uniquely as a pairwise coprime product of atomic prime-power birth moduli forming a witness cover whose support spans the prime coordinates of~$n$. This yields the bound $ (m) (n)$ for every minimal generator $m$ and a primitive-versus-ladder dichotomy for atomic factors. The arithmetic increment here is a finite rank-checkable nonemptiness criterion for the three-coordinate witness families; together with the one- and two-coordinate cases, this gives complete classifications of \( M_n\) for \( (n) 3\). We also show that both $B_n$ and its minimal-generator set admit unique factorizations into connected coordinate blocks, producing partition-lattice fo...
